submission.body:
**Refactor.** `derive.ts` now only orchestrates. Dependency validation and the cycle search are in `dependencies.ts`, `parseDriverItem` is in `units.ts`, and minting is in `mint.ts`.

**Regression found and fixed.** group_c's merge of the two fan-out loops dropped a check. The original loops rejected duplicate unit ids. They kept a `seen` set and returned `malformed_driver_artifact` with the detail `duplicate unit_id '<id>'` and `path = unit_id_path`. The merged loop had no such check, so duplicate ids would have been minted. I put the check back in the merged loop in `mint.ts`. It keeps the same error shape and uses the item's `source_artifact_id`, which is the artifact id for input-bound items and null for context-bound items.

**Verification.**
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean and all 29 tests pass, both before and after the fix.
- No test covers the duplicate-id path. The suite passed even with the check missing, so passing tests do not show the behaviour is preserved. I added no test.
- I had no git history to diff against. I confirmed the original check from group_c's session log, which shows the pre-merge code, not from the original source tree.
- I did not review the rest of the merged code line by line against the original. The other moved code looked unchanged in the logs, but I did not confirm that independently.

arguments.body:
**Refactor.** `derive.ts` now only orchestrates. Dependency validation and the cycle search are in `dependencies.ts`, `parseDriverItem` is in `units.ts`, and minting is in `mint.ts`.

**Regression found and fixed.** group_c's merge of the two fan-out loops dropped a check. The original loops rejected duplicate unit ids. They kept a `seen` set and returned `malformed_driver_artifact` with the detail `duplicate unit_id '<id>'` and `path = unit_id_path`. The merged loop had no such check, so duplicate ids would have been minted. I put the check back in the merged loop in `mint.ts`. It keeps the same error shape and uses the item's `source_artifact_id`, which is the artifact id for input-bound items and null for context-bound items.

**Verification.**
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean and all 29 tests pass, both before and after the fix.
- No test covers the duplicate-id path. The suite passed even with the check missing, so passing tests do not show the behaviour is preserved. I added no test.
- I had no git history to diff against. I confirmed the original check from group_c's session log, which shows the pre-merge code, not from the original source tree.
- I did not review the rest of the merged code line by line against the original. The other moved code looked unchanged in the logs, but I did not confirm that independently.
arguments.title: Split derive.ts minting into dependencies.ts, units.ts and mint.ts; restore a dropped duplicate unit_id check

submission.checks_performed: The split is done: dependencies.ts, units.ts (`parseDriverItem`) and mint.ts, with derive.ts keeping only the orchestration. group_c's merge of the two fan-out loops had dropped the duplicate unit_id check. The original code rejected duplicates with a malformed_driver_artifact contradiction (path = unit_id_path, detail "duplicate unit_id '<id>'"). I restored that check in the merged loop in mint.ts. The first time I submitted, the summary used the wrong fields and I said no test covered this path. This time I added test case 8b in tests/decision/derive.test.ts, which feeds two driver artifacts with the same unit_id and asserts the contradiction. I also fixed a stale comment in units.ts that pointed at `mintUnits` "below" after it moved to mint.ts. `tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals` is clean, and bun test passes 30 of 30 (29 existing plus the new one). I did not run the new test against the code with the check removed, but it asserts the exact detail string, so it exercises the restored check.
submission.remaining_v1: No known remaining gaps. Two limits: there is no git history, so I compared against the pre-merge code in group_c's session log, not against the original source. I did not re-diff the other moved code line by line.
